fluff.overview: The Kage ("shadow") light battle armor was one of the first Draconis Combine designs to enter production following the Truce of Tukayyid. Developed jointly by Internal Security Force scientists and Draconis Elite Strike Team advisers, the suit was built for reconnaissance, infiltration, and intelligence gathering in hostile environments. Produced by New Samarkand Metals and Luthien Armor Works, the Kage entered service in 3056 as a replacement for the older DEST Infiltration Suit, offering far greater protection and mobility. The design earned a strong reputation within DCMS special operations and line formations alike for its exceptional aerial agility and advanced stealth characteristics.
fluff.capabilities:
The vibro-claw Kage replaces both armored gloves with vibro-claws, trading manipulation capability and all weapon mounts for lethal close-combat effectiveness. The suit carries no anti-personnel weapon mount and no squad support weapon, making it entirely dependent on melee range engagement. It retains the standard 750-kilogram mass, 275 kilograms of basic stealth armor with electronic and infrared suppression, and the partial wing assembly providing 120-meter assisted jumps with a retractable profile.

The vibro-claws are devastating against unarmored targets and can damage lighter battle armor suits in close quarters. Combined with the Kage's stealth and aerial mobility, troopers can close to melee range before opponents can react, striking from unexpected angles. The complete absence of ranged weaponry is a significant liability if the team is detected at distance, and the loss of armored gloves limits the troopers' ability to perform non-combat tasks such as climbing, carrying equipment, or handling prisoners.
fluff.deployment: Clan Nova Cat organized vibro-claw Kage suits into five-trooper Points for close-combat operations. The melee-only configuration appealed to warriors who valued personal combat, though the complete lack of ranged weaponry limited the variant's tactical flexibility compared to standard Clan battle armor designs.
fluff.history:
Research and development of the Kage began in March 3051 as a joint project between Internal Security Force scientists and Draconis Elite Strike Team advisers. The program grew from a failed prototype of the Raiden battle armor, repurposing its chassis for a dedicated reconnaissance and infiltration role. First prototypes appeared in May 3052, but the design team quickly encountered a serious problem. DCMS commanders had demanded a suit capable of outjumping most BattleMechs, and the jump jet configuration necessary to achieve those distances produced dangerously unstable flight characteristics. Several test operators were killed before engineers devised a solution: a partial wing with stabilizing fins that could retract flush against the suit when not in use. This redesign consumed three and a half additional years of development before mass production finally commenced in March 3056.

The Kage entered service as a direct replacement for the DEST Infiltration Suit, and within years it had virtually displaced the older sneak suit across Combine special operations units. Where the Infiltration Suit provided stealth alone, the Kage combined infiltration capability with enough armor and mobility to survive contact with powered opponents. Regular DCMS line formations also received Kage suits, employing them primarily as forward observers and artillery spotters for Arrow IV batteries using light TAG designators.

One of the suit's earliest high-profile deployments came during Operation Serpent, the Inner Sphere's strike against the Clan Smoke Jaguar homeworld of Huntress. Three DEST teams wearing Kage suits infiltrated the planet's surface with orders to destroy the command and control center coordinating orbital defenses. The teams overcame Elemental guards at the facility and completed their mission, clearing the way for the invasion fleet to press the attack. The Kage's stealth and jump capability proved critical in allowing the teams to bypass ground-level security and approach the target undetected.

During the Jihad, Kage-equipped DEST operatives carried out another critical operation in 3069, extracting Hohiro Kurita from Word of Blake captivity. That same year saw brutal fighting on Luthien itself, where a close-combat variant armed with vibro-claws appeared for the first time. These weaponless but lethally equipped suits proved effective against unarmored targets in the close quarters of urban combat. Luthien Armor Works had begun producing this variant, but the plant was destroyed mere months after the production line opened. New Samarkand Metals continued as the primary source for all Kage production through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, adding a space operations variant designed for boarding actions and the experimental Kage C, which incorporated advanced stealth technology salvaged from captured Blakist suits along with a networked sensor system to enhance the Kage's value within coordinated formations.

The Kage remained a cornerstone of Combine special operations capability through the Republic era and beyond. Its combination of stealth, aerial agility, and compact size ensured continued demand even as newer battle armor designs entered service. DCMS doctrine continued to favor Kage teams for deep reconnaissance, target designation, and sabotage missions where heavier suits would compromise operational security.
